title: Does a heritable aggression gene evolve higher under food scarcity?
question: When food is scarce, does natural selection favour agents whose frustration translates more strongly into attack?
background: Agents inherit an aggression gain: how strongly frustration (accumulated negative reward-prediction error) drives their attack population. Attacking steals energy from a neighbour. Resource-defence theory predicts that aggression pays when resources are contested, but very scarce resources may not be worth defending. Both outcomes are plausible.

hypotheses.statement: The aggression gene evolves higher under scarcity
Agents attack more often under scarcity
Under scarcity, attacks are more likely when a neighbour is in reach
